subject: Intermittent outbound failures after private deploy — possible SNAT/session pinning
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@atlasbank.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: netops@atlasbank.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Outbound failures after private deploy — intermittent 502s

Hi Grace / Redwood team,

We completed the Private deployment cutover over the weekend for AtlasBank (production VPCs routed over the new on-prem gateway). Since the cutover we see intermittent outbound failures from app tier to external payment service (502 / connection reset). The failures are sporadic — roughly 1-3% of requests, most common during peak windows.

What we see:
- Backend app logs show a series of TCP retransmits followed by connection resets.
- Failures are more frequent for a subset of internal source subnets (10.12.3.0/24).
- We recently adjusted egress firewall MTU to 1400 during a security appliance firmware update (was 1500 previously).
- No obvious capacity pressure on gateway CPU or memory.

Attached: short pcap capture from an app host showing the reset sequence (atlasbank_outbound.pcap) and a traceroute to the payment service.

Can the Redwood private deployment team take a look? We can give a maintenance window if changes are needed.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Jenkins
Network Operations — AtlasBank
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@atlasbank.com>

Subject: Re: Outbound failures after private deploy — intermittent 502s

Hi Sam — thanks for the report and the capture. Sorry you're seeing this after cutover.

I'll triage immediately and loop in our on-call network lead (Markus) and private deployments lead (Vanessa). Quick asks to help speed debugging:
- Can you share the pcap and the host IP of the app that captured it (so we can correlate conntrack entries)?
- A short output of `sudo conntrack -L | grep <app-ip>` from the gateway would be helpful if you can provide it.
- Confirm whether the egress path uses ECMP (multiple uplinks) or a single active peer.

We'll get back with a hypothesis and a suggested remediation window.

- Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Manager — Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound failures after private deploy — intermittent 502s

FYI initial look: symptoms smell like SNAT/session pinning + asymmetric egress. Two quick possibilities:

1) SNAT pool imbalance or ephemeral port exhaustion on the active NAT device causing packet resets when state gets orphaned.
2) ECMP / asymmetric routing where the SYN goes out one egress path and the SYN/ACK returns via another, leading to NAT mismatch at the backend (or the appliance rewriting source ports inconsistently).

If the customer changed MTU at the firewall, we should also consider fragmentation causing path MTU issues — but the reset/retransmit pattern in Sam's note points more toward session state mismatch.

Action items I recommend before a maintenance window:
- Request short conntrack dump from the gateway for the app IP range. I attached a sample conntrack-summary.txt from a similar case.
- Confirm ephemeral port range and current SNAT pool size on the appliance.
- If ECMP is in play, collect 5-tuple hash distribution (src/dst/ip/port/proto) to see if flows are being steered inconsistently.

I'll prepare a short playbook: either tighten egress to a single SNAT hop (consistent NAT) or implement source-based routing so reply path matches ingress.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Network Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: conntrack-summary.txt (text)

Thanks Markus/Grace — attaching the full pcap and the traceroute I ran from the app host (traceroute-10.0.3.1.txt).

Notes:
- App host: 10.12.3.42 (host captured pcap).
- We do have ECMP across two transit peers (peer-A and peer-B) for egress. We believed the NAT appliance would be handling session consolidation, but it looks like source ports change depending on the egress peer.
- MTU clamp change to 1400 happened on the firewall between 03:00-03:30 UTC on 2027-07-18; we didn't see obvious packet loss before the cutover.

If you need elevated logs from the appliance I can pull them (we may need vendor approval).

-Sam

Attachments: atlasbank_outbound.pcap (pcap), traceroute-10.0.3.1.txt (text)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: sam.jenkins@atlasbank.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound failures after private deploy — intermittent 502s

I pulled the pcap and ran a quick correlation with the gateway conntrack. Summary of what I see:

- There are SYNs from 10.12.3.42 to the payment service where the initial packet leaves via peer-A and the SYN/ACK returns via peer-B. When that happens, the NAT device maps a different ephemeral port on the return path, so the app host sees a TCP reset.
- Conntrack shows short-lived state entries and a small number of retransmits aligned with the observed resets.
- The firewall MTU reduction to 1400 is causing some MSS adjustments but not the primary reset mode here — the reset correlates tightly to flows that traverse different egress peers.

Two remediation options (ordered by risk):
1) Reduce ECMP to a single egress peer for the affected subnets (quick mitigation) — fixes consistency but reduces available bandwidth.
2) Configure a consistent SNAT egress point: ensure SNAT is performed on a single device for the app subnet (preferred long-term). This can be achieved by adjusting route preferences or adding a source-based routing policy that pins source subnets to a SNAT-capable hop.

Suggested maintenance window: Wed 07/21 02:00-04:00 UTC to:
- Apply source-based routing on the gateway for 10.12.3.0/24
- Increase SNAT ephemeral port range (vendor appliance) to avoid port reuse during cutover
- Apply MTU clamp of 1400 on the NAT device to avoid in-flight fragmentation surprises

I'll prepare the playbook and a rollback plan (small iptables changes + route preference change). Linking our internal runbook: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/private-egress-snat-playbook

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Private Deployments Lead — Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: sam.jenkins@atlasbank.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound failures after private deploy — intermittent 502s

Thanks all. Plan below and action owners:

Planned window: Thu 2027-07-22 02:00-04:00 UTC (customer approved)
Actions:
- Vanessa: deploy source-based routing policy + set SNAT on designated egress hop for 10.12.3.0/24; test synthetic flows and monitor conntrack for orphaned entries.
- Markus: increase ephemeral port range on the appliance and validate no port exhaustion. Provide rollback steps to revert SNAT changes.
- Karthik: coordinate with AtlasBank to pull vendor logs if needed and to validate MTU clamp on the NAT device.
- Sam: confirm vendor window and provide appliance admin creds for logs (if approved).

I'll be the point of contact during the window and will watch error rates and latency. If the source-based routing doesn't remove failures we'll move to single-egress for a subset of hosts and iterate.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Manager — Redwood Inference
